title: Question 1.1
statement_text: For which $\varepsilon>0$ and $k>0$ does there exist a bound $c$ such that each simple graph $G$ with minimum degree at least $\varepsilon|V(G)|$ either contains $C_{2k+1}$ as a subgraph or $\chi(G)\leq c$ (or both)?
context_text: The undirected question goes back to Erdős and Simonovits (1972), who asked whether graphs with no fixed odd cycle and large minimum degree have bounded chromatic number, for $C_3$ and $C_5$. Erdős, Hajnal and Simonovits showed that for $C_3$ no bound exists if $\varepsilon<1/3$; Thomassen answered affirmatively for $C_3$ when $\varepsilon>1/3$ and for all longer odd cycles for every $\varepsilon>0$ (Brandt and Thomassé showed triangle-free graphs with minimum degree at least $|V(G)|/3$ are even $4$-colourable), and for even cycles an affirmative answer follows from a result of Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (large graphs with linearly many edges contain large complete bipartite subgraphs). The general version for any fixed forbidden graph, the chromatic threshold, was completely resolved by Allen, Böttcher, Griffiths, Kohayakawa and Morris. Thus the question is fully answered in the literature: such a bound exists if and only if $k\ge2$, or $k=1$ and $\varepsilon\ge1/3$. The paper studies a directed analogue, and its main theorem (via replacing each edge by two anti-parallel arcs) recovers Thomassen's result for odd cycles of length at least five.
notes: Presented as background context; the specific cases addressed by Thomassen [11,12] are resolved, but the fully general formulation is posed by the paper authors as a unifying question.
paper_title: Orientations of cycles in digraphs of high chromatic number and high minimum out-degree

title: Question 1.2
statement_text: Which orientations of cycles are contained in every digraph (without loops or parallel arcs) with high minimum out-degree (at least $\varepsilon|V(D)|$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$) and high chromatic number?
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but may have anti-parallel arcs (directed $2$-cycles); $\chi(D)$ is the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph, and $H$ is contained in $D$ if it is a subdigraph. An orientation of a graph $G$ picks exactly one of the arcs $uv,vu$ for each edge $uv$. A block of an orientation $C$ of a cycle is a maximal connected subdigraph containing no $\rightarrow\leftarrow$ or $\leftarrow\rightarrow$, i.e. a maximal directed subpath (a directed cycle has a single block); its length is its number of arcs. The authors' main theorem: for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $k\ge2$ and an orientation $C$ of a $k$-cycle, there is $c\ge1$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\chi(D)\ge c$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon|V(D)|$ contains $C$ if and only if $C$ has at least three blocks, or two blocks both of length at least two; the negative direction uses directed shift graphs augmented to have large minimum out-degree. This question, the directed analogue of the chromatic threshold of cycles, is thus fully answered in the same paper. By reversing arcs the theorem also holds for high minimum in-degree, and by doubling edges it implies Thomassen's undirected result for odd cycles of length at least five. The undirected question goes back to Erdős and Simonovits (1972), who asked whether graphs with no fixed odd cycle and large minimum degree have bounded chromatic number, for $C_3$ and $C_5$. Erdős, Hajnal and Simonovits showed that for $C_3$ no bound exists if $\varepsilon<1/3$; Thomassen answered affirmatively for $C_3$ when $\varepsilon>1/3$ and for all longer odd cycles for every $\varepsilon>0$ (Brandt and Thomassé showed triangle-free graphs with minimum degree at least $|V(G)|/3$ are even $4$-colourable), and for even cycles an affirmative answer follows from a result of Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (large graphs with linearly many edges contain large complete bipartite subgraphs). The general version for any fixed forbidden graph, the chromatic threshold, was completely resolved by Allen, Böttcher, Griffiths, Kohayakawa and Morris.
notes: This question is fully resolved within the same paper by Theorem 1.3; included because it is a labelled question environment and the central research question.

title: Question 4.1
statement_text: For which fixed digraphs $H$ does there exist a constant $c_{\varepsilon}\geq 1$ for all $\varepsilon>0$ such that every digraph $D$ without loops or parallel arcs with $\chi(D)\geq c_{\varepsilon}$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon|V(D)|$ contains $H$ as a subdigraph?
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but may have anti-parallel arcs (directed $2$-cycles); $\chi(D)$ is the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph, and $H$ is contained in $D$ if it is a subdigraph. An orientation of a graph $G$ picks exactly one of the arcs $uv,vu$ for each edge $uv$. A block of an orientation $C$ of a cycle is a maximal connected subdigraph containing no $\rightarrow\leftarrow$ or $\leftarrow\rightarrow$, i.e. a maximal directed subpath (a directed cycle has a single block); its length is its number of arcs. The authors' main theorem: for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $k\ge2$ and an orientation $C$ of a $k$-cycle, there is $c\ge1$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\chi(D)\ge c$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon|V(D)|$ contains $C$ if and only if $C$ has at least three blocks, or two blocks both of length at least two; the negative direction uses directed shift graphs augmented to have large minimum out-degree. So the main theorem answers this question for orientations of cycles. Since every sufficiently large graph with a linear number of edges contains a large complete bipartite subgraph (Alon, Krivelevich, Sudakov), a Ramsey-type argument colouring arcs by their direction between the two sides gives a large complete bipartite subdigraph with all arcs oriented from one side to the other; hence the answer is affirmative for every subdigraph $H$ of such a uniformly oriented complete bipartite digraph. Directed cycles, and orientations of cycles obtained from a directed cycle by reversing a single arc, are negative examples.
paper_title: Orientations of cycles in digraphs of high chromatic number and high minimum out-degree

title: Question 4.2
statement_text: For a fixed digraph $H$, what is the minimum value $\varepsilon_{H}\geq 0$ such that there exists a constant $c\geq 1$ such that every digraph $D$ without loops or parallel arcs with $\chi(D)\geq c$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon_{H}|V(D)|$ contains $H$ as a subdigraph?
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but may have anti-parallel arcs (directed $2$-cycles); $\chi(D)$ is the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph, and $H$ is contained in $D$ if it is a subdigraph. An orientation of a graph $G$ picks exactly one of the arcs $uv,vu$ for each edge $uv$. A block of an orientation $C$ of a cycle is a maximal connected subdigraph containing no $\rightarrow\leftarrow$ or $\leftarrow\rightarrow$, i.e. a maximal directed subpath (a directed cycle has a single block); its length is its number of arcs. The authors' main theorem: for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $k\ge2$ and an orientation $C$ of a $k$-cycle, there is $c\ge1$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\chi(D)\ge c$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon|V(D)|$ contains $C$ if and only if $C$ has at least three blocks, or two blocks both of length at least two; the negative direction uses directed shift graphs augmented to have large minimum out-degree. The question is well defined for every digraph $H$, since the statement trivially holds with $\varepsilon_H=1$. The quantity $\varepsilon_H$ is a directed analogue of the chromatic threshold of undirected graphs (for which the general problem was resolved by Allen, Böttcher, Griffiths, Kohayakawa and Morris; e.g. it is $1/3$ for the triangle by Erdős–Hajnal–Simonovits and Thomassen), and the main theorem characterises the orientations of cycles with $\varepsilon_H=0$. The authors also suggest variants of these questions where large chromatic number is replaced by large dichromatic number (the minimum number of acyclic sets, i.e. inducing no directed cycle, partitioning $V(D)$, introduced by Neumann-Lara).
notes: The authors note that $\varepsilon_H = 1$ is always an upper bound, so the quantity is well-defined for all digraphs $H$.
paper_title: Orientations of cycles in digraphs of high chromatic number and high minimum out-degree
